projects_portfolio: The site you are on right now, and the one I keep coming back to. It gathers my skills and the projects I have built over the years, personal, academic and professional, and has grown up alongside me since my very first lines of code.
projects_filestorage: A place to keep your files without handing them over to the giants of the web and their questionable privacy policies. Upload, share and find your documents from any device: the storage service I wished I had, and one of the projects closest to my heart.
projects_sourceconsole: Running a game server should not require being an expert. This console lets you administer servers for Garry's Mod, Counter-Strike: Source, Team Fortress 2 and other Source engine games from a simple web page, even without access to the server itself.
projects_mangaparadise: A showcase website I built on a voluntary basis for Manga Paradise, an association of manga and Japanese culture enthusiasts. It replaced their outdated website and gave the association a fresh window onto its activities and its community.
projects_terminalhomepage: A home page that looks like a command terminal, for those of us who are a little nerdy. Type a few commands to reach my portfolio, my social media or my personal projects: a playful gateway, best enjoyed with a keyboard.
projects_ravenshortener: A link shortener that respects you: simple to use, secure and customizable down to the last detail, without trading away your privacy. One of the projects I am proudest of, and one that other services can build upon.
projects_onlineresume: My resume, reimagined as a website. Pleasant to read for recruiters, easy to keep up to date, and just as clear on a computer, a phone or a printed sheet of paper.
projects_timeloop: Born after losing someone close to me, a reminder of how precious time is. It counts the time left until a date to come, or elapsed since a moment that mattered, including major historical events, so you never forget how fast time flies.
projects_blog: My personal corner of the web, where I share my thoughts, experiences and discoveries about computer science and everything else that sparks my curiosity. No set format, no imposed topic: just a place to write freely.
projects_magicanswers: Inspired by the book of the same name: ask a question, get an answer vague enough to fit any situation. Designed with a UX/UI designer, with care so that everyone can use it, and without cookies, tracking or any data collected.
projects_terminalstories: An interactive story reader in the style of computer terminals from another era. Every choice shapes how the story unfolds, whether the tale was written by hand or imagined on the fly by an artificial intelligence, and an encyclopedia lets you explore each universe, its characters and its places.
projects_pericles: An encyclopedia in the spirit of Wikipedia for building and documenting a fictional universe, the tool I would have loved to have back in my role-playing days. Linked pages, a timeline and live events, all kept in your own browser, with no account and no remote server.
